_notes: Dusk on the rooftops. The vole hunt that teaches Ferocity, and the choice of what to do with a gift that will not be given.
Scenes 0-5 of the prologue as it was before the split; `--scene story:<index>` still counts across the whole prologue, not within this file.

lines: Dusk over Hollowmere. The lamps going up, one by one, like the city buttoning its coat.
She puts the kettle on when the lamps go up. I am punctual. She is predictable. The arrangement works, and has worked for fifteen years, which is a long time in a cat.
Tonight calls for a gift. A vole, ideally. Voles say what flowers cannot.

scenes.art_desc: Ash pressed low on rooftop tiles, stalking an unaware vole near a chimney pot, warm dusk light
lines: There. Under the chimney pot. Fat, smug, unaware.
I go low. The tiles are still day-warm under my belly and the wind is blowing the wrong way for the vole.
There is a red feeling that lives at the bottom of a cat, older than cities. It is the one part of me that has not aged.
I wait longer than I once needed to. Waiting is cheap. The other thing is not.

notes: ❋ FEROCITY, the red energy — the oldest there is, and the only one a cat is born knowing. It pays for POUNCE.

coach.text: The opposition. Tonight: one vole of tremendous conviction.
Its life is a red thread. Claws do the unstitching.
It telegraphs its next move here. Honesty is its one virtue.
Your hand is ENERGY — tonight, all Ferocity.
Paws are actions. Placing an energy anywhere spends one. Three a turn.
Two empty pips, two Ferocity owed. Feed it one.
One to go. A skill fires only once every pip is filled.
Full. A willing card. Tap USE.
Four off its thread — that is what a powered card buys.
And the spool — energy still wound in your deck — is two lighter. It only unwinds. Spent stays spent.
A breath left in it. SCRATCH — free, once a turn. Finish politely.

lines: Acquired. Thoughtfully dead. Arranged neatly, carried gently.
I sat afterward longer than the work deserved, and did not mention it to anybody.
She will say 'not on the table', and mean 'thank you'. She has said it every time. I have put it on the table every time.
The vole declines to be a gift tonight, and I decline to argue the point at my age.
She will have to make do with my company. I sat with that a while before I could agree to it.
The rooftop road home, and the evening going purple at its edges.

There is a gap over the alley at Cooper's that I used to cross without consulting anybody, including myself. I stood at the edge of it and counted the four seconds she taught me, and went round by the wall instead.
I spent that hour thinking about a sunbeam I remember from March. I want that noted. Whatever else the record says of me, let it say I was happy.
